title: Egg omelet or scrambled egg with potatoes and/or onions, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of eggs, boiled or baked potatoes and onions, prepared without added oil or other fats. Eggs provide high‑quality protein, while potatoes and onions supply carbohydrates, fiber, vitamins and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are often called a “complete food” because they contain all essential amino acids.
Potatoes are one of the world’s most consumed vegetables and are rich in vitamin C and potassium.
Onions contain sulfur compounds that give them their characteristic aroma and have antioxidant properties.
Cooking without fat preserves the natural taste of the ingredients and results in a low‑energy‑density meal.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: One serving provides about 6 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Rich in vitamin D and B12
items.content: The yolk supplies vitamin D, while both yolk and white contain vitamin B12, important for the nervous system.

items.title: Potassium and magnesium
items.content: Potatoes and onions are good sources of potassium and magnesium, which help heart and muscle function.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Potato skins and onions add fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Low added fat
items.content: Absence of oil reduces saturated fat and overall calorie content.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg proteins.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: The yolk contains cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should consume in moderation.

items.title: Solanine in potatoes
items.content: Green spots or sprouts can contain solanine, a toxin that should be avoided.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Boil or bake potatoes until tender, dice them. Sauté onions in a dry pan until golden (add a splash of water if needed). Beat the eggs, pour them over the vegetables, and stir continuously until the mixture sets. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The dish is best eaten fresh. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat with a little water to prevent drying out.
